Yes. A truly massive story. This will go down in history.

AP is a wire service - one of the 3 main ones in the world - which means they discover news, then other news outlets report on it. This is something they think will be interesting enough such that newspapers, TV, etc will be interested in it. Bigstory is the domain they use for basically everything that's not sports. It's less that they consider it a "big story" that everyone should see and more they consider it a "big story" that a variety of other news organizations will be interested in (for better or worse).

If your TV has PC, use that FOR GAMES

  1. Internal processing - PC mode should disable any extra processing.
  2. Color space - so back in the day, luminosity was given values of 16-235 because equipment was not quite as precise. The full range was 0-255. Anything below 16 was ignored. Anything above 235 was ignored. PCs came out and things were better so they used the full range - 0-255. Television to this day uses the narrower range, meaning output from a PC will ALWAYS be fuller when the source is non-TV/blu-ray.

For high-quality movies or TV like blu-ray or something, you may want to switch to a different input or use a different device entirely and configure it for MOVIE/FILM/CINEMA mode and to set your color temperature as close to 6500K as possible (daylight).
